For example, if we draw a horizontal line, we get the following model representing [MATH: \dfrac24\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/c5b951e11b2749f1e4402faef6be392c]

Content:
We can continue to split the fraction into equal parts to generate more equivalent fractions.

Content:
For example, if we draw two more horizontal lines, we get a model representing [MATH: \dfrac48\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/686a5efee4b2a74a9cfe0d43fa1afbe9]

Content:
Therefore, the following fractions are all equivalent:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac12, \qquad \dfrac24, \qquad \dfrac48]

Content:
Watch Out! Whenever we split a fraction model into more equal parts to generate equivalent fractions, all parts must have the same area!

Item 10 — Tutorial: Creating Equivalent Fractions Using Fewer Parts

Content:
We can also create equivalent fractions by removing some parts, where possible.

Content:
For example, let's look at the following fraction, representing [MATH: \dfrac24\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/1841033cf1c017365c227d7decb2b446]

Content:
If we remove the horizontal line, we'll generate an equivalent fraction representing [MATH: \dfrac12\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/529c11a4a1acb79ae3a764f6480c3742]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude once again that the following fractions are equivalent:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac12, \qquad \dfrac24]

Item 11 — Example: Determining an Equivalent Fraction Given a Fraction Model

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/1beda2ef2e7e203f71dcb19c00b478ff]

The fraction given below is equivalent to the fraction shown in the picture. What number is missing?

[MATH: 0]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
There are [MATH: 4] equal parts in the given shape in total. Of them, [MATH: 3] parts are shaded. So, [MATH: \dfrac{3}{4}] of the shape is shaded.

Since we are looking for a fraction of the form [MATH: 0], we now draw another shape that has the same shaded area but is divided into [MATH: 8] equal parts. To do that, we subdivide each part into [MATH: 2] equal pieces:

[IMG: /graphics/16fd3a447b5ffcdddfe8f6418107e25a]

The shape on the right is divided into [MATH: 8] equal parts. Of them, [MATH: 6] parts are shaded. So, [MATH: \dfrac{6}{8}] of the shape is shaded.

Hence, we obtain
[MATH: 6]

Therefore, the missing number is [MATH: \color{blue}6.]
